hypotheses.claim: Exact lexical relevance can use the canonical inverted-index posting counts and one pre-tokenized query without changing retrieval semantics.
hypotheses.change: Reused posting counts, computed each candidate relevance once, and removed per-candidate content tokenization from filtering and sorting.
hypotheses.semantic_risk_control: The candidate pool, tag boost, exclusion policy, score tuple, and deterministic tie-break are unchanged; frozen selected-result hashes and indexed/fallback equivalence tests pass.

hypotheses.claim: Conversation context assembly can resolve selected item IDs through the current canonical knowledge index instead of rebuilding an O(N) item map for every query.
hypotheses.change: Used index by-id offsets when the index fingerprint is current and retained the original full-scan fallback for stale or unindexed packs.
hypotheses.semantic_risk_control: Index freshness is checked on every query; fallback output is covered by exact equivalence tests.

scale_observations.interpretation: Retrieval and context-query latency remain bounded enough for the release study; corpus construction memory remains linear and is a documented future optimization target, not hidden as a pass.

safe_slimming.reason: Static reachability alone cannot prove public, CLI, plugin, or reflection-based code is obsolete. Compatibility surfaces remain classified rather than silently deleted.
